newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan construction shares up on central bank move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan construction shares up on central bank move.

text.p: Taiwan's construction shares were outperforming the wider market at mid-morning on Monday, boosted by the central bank's decision at the weekend to scrap selective credit controls on land, brokers said.
After 90 minutes, the construction sector had gained 1.37 percent while the overall index was up a mere 0.10 percent.
Prince Housing was up 70 cents or 2.76 percent to T$26.1 and Cathay Construction had gained 50 cents or 1.04 percent to T$48.8.
"The latest liberalisation gives a boost to the sluggish real estate industry," said Chen Han-chung of Yungli Securities.
But Michael Chien of China Securities cautioned the rise in the construction shares may only be temporary.
"It is still too early to say whether the central bank's new medicine will cure the real estate industry," Chien said.

The selective credit controls were put in place in March 1989 after money supply growth surged and real estate prices rocketed. During 1987 and 1989, land speculation sent real estate prices rocketing more than 300 percent in most cities.
The controls were designed to prevent too much money from flowing into land speculation.
The central bank has incrementally relaxed the controls seven times since 1989 as the property sector has cooled.
